title: hardware-comparison-benchmarks-a100-h100-l40s-2026-03-05
content:
Summary:

This working doc captures the most recent hardware comparison runs between A100, H100, and L40S variants across cloud SKUs and driver/CUDA combinations. Primary goal: identify practical performance deltas for our serving runtime (fp16/bf16/quantized paths), surface any driver-induced regressions, and recommend default SKUs + driver versions for Hosted and Dedicated offerings.

High-level takeaways (short):
- H100 (CUDA 12.1, driver 545.x) shows the best end-to-end throughput on long-context workloads (seq_len>=2048) — ~20–30% higher tokens/sec vs A100 (CUDA 11.8) on equivalent SKUs when using bf16/tensor-core kernels.
- A100 remains competitive for short-context and latency-sensitive single-request workloads due to lower tail latency and slightly better p50 for small batches.
- L40S (NVL/S cloud SKUs) performs well for throughput-bound workloads with large batch sizes, but is more memory-bandwidth bound; on some SKUs it matches H100 throughput when using int8/bitsandbytes quantized models.
- Driver/CUDA matters: CUDA 12.x improves H100 tensor-core kernels but introduced a small (~5–10%) regression on some A100 attention kernels in our builds — likely cuBLAS/cuTensor changes.

Test matrix (short):
- GPUs: NVIDIA A100 (40GB), A100 (80GB), H100 (80GB), L40S (48GB)
- Cloud SKUs: GCP a2-highgpu variants, AWS p4d.24xlarge / p5 / g5dn (L40S-like), Azure NDas_v4 (H100), Oracle/other where applicable — SKU names recorded per run logs.
- Drivers/CUDA: CUDA 11.8 + driver 525.x; CUDA 12.0 + driver 535.x; CUDA 12.1 + driver 545.x.
- Model family: 7B and 13B decoder-only transformer test models (fp16, bf16 where supported, and 8-bit quantized with bitsandbytes), and a medium encoder-only embedding model for throughput sanity checks.
- Workloads: interactive single-request (batch=1) seq_len 512 & 1024; streaming chat style seq_len 2048 with chunked generation; throughput tests with steady batch sizes 4, 8, 16 and sequence lengths 512, 1024, 2048; KV cache hot-start tests.
- Metrics collected: p50/p95 latency (ms), tokens/sec (steady-state), GPU utilization (nvidia-smi), SM active %, memory bandwidth utilization (Nsight/metrics), kernel timing (Nsight Systems + CUPTI traces), host-to-device PCIe latency.

Methodology notes (repro):
- All runs executed from identical AMI/container image built from ci/benchmarks:commit-sha listed in linked artifacts.
- Warm-up: 3000 tokens of synthetic warm-up before measuring steady-state to populate KV caches.
- Measurement window: 120s steady-state; tokens/sec computed by dividing produced tokens by wall time after warm-up.
- Profiling: Nsight Systems for end-to-end traces (collection of 3 seeds), Nsight Compute for kernel-level hotspots on a representative timestep.
- Variability control: runs repeated 3–5x; we capture min/median/max; p95 calculated across all measured requests.

Results highlights (selected):
- 13B model, bf16, seq_len=2048, batch=8:
  - H100 (CUDA 12.1 / driver 545.45): 145k tokens/sec steady-state, p50 gen latency per request: 98 ms, p95: 180 ms.
  - A100 (CUDA 11.8 / driver 525.89): 112k tokens/sec steady-state, p50: 110 ms, p95: 220 ms.
  - L40S (CUDA 12.1 / driver 545.45): 130k tokens/sec steady-state, p50: 105 ms, p95: 210 ms.
- 7B model, fp16, seq_len=1024, batch=4 (latency focus):
  - A100: p50 48 ms, p95 92 ms
  - H100: p50 52 ms, p95 100 ms (H100 slightly higher p50 for small batches — kernel launch overhead observed)
  - L40S: p50 50 ms, p95 96 ms
- Quantized (8-bit) 13B, seq_len=2048, batch=16 throughput run:
  - L40S int8 path: 310k tokens/sec (best-case for cost-optimized SKU)
  - H100 int8-ish path (we used bfloat16 optimized kernels, not hardware int8): 280k tokens/sec
  - A100: 240k tokens/sec

Profiling observations (details):
- H100: tensor core attention + fused MHA kernels show highest utilization; Nsight traces show fewer kernel launches and better overlapping of memcpy and compute on CUDA 12.1. SM occupancy consistently high for bf16 path.
- A100: attention kernel latency slightly higher, and we see more frequent kernel serialization on CUDA 12.x builds. Using CUDA 11.8 + driver 525 gave more stable attention kernel times on A100.
- L40S: memory bandwidth is the limiting factor for large batches and long contexts; cuBLAS GEMM performance is good but staging and host-device transfers matter in p95.
- All GPUs: small-batch, short-seq paths dominated by kernel startup/enqueue overhead (host-side). For those, our executor overhead (thread scheduling + Python/async glue) appears proportionally larger.

Driver/CUDA specific notes (actionable):
- CUDA 12.1 + driver 545.x appears to be the best default for H100 SKUs (Azure NDas_v4) — we recommend standardizing on this for H100 offerings.
- For A100-heavy fleets (Dedicated/older clusters), CUDA 11.8 + driver 525.x remains the safest baseline. CUDA 12.x showed small regressions on some attention kernels; we filed ENG-1247 to investigate cuBLAS/cuTensor differences.
- L40S tested successfully on CUDA 12.1; suggest we validate node images in Hosted with driver 545.x and fallback configs for customers on older drivers.

Anomalies / open questions:
- One A100 SKU (gcp a2-highgpu-1g) showed sporadic p95 spikes tied to preemption/re-scheduling on host — need to confirm cloud host isolation and hypervisor config.
- A small but reproducible ~5% perf delta between two A100 80GB SKUs on different cloud providers — likely driver/firmware differences.
- Bitsandbytes quantized kernel on H100 shows occasional correctness warnings in one build (nonblocking) — tracking with Miguel.

Recommendations (short-term):
- Default recommended stacks:
  - H100 SKUs: CUDA 12.1 + driver 545.x, runtime build with bf16-optimized kernels enabled.
  - A100 SKUs: CUDA 11.8 + driver 525.x until we resolve the cuBLAS/cuTensor regressions in CUDA 12.x (ENG-1247).
  - L40S: CUDA 12.1 + driver 545.x for Hosted throughput-optimized tiers, with explicit memory-bandwidth tuning for large-batch workloads.
- Add per-SKU perf profiles into the model catalog so runtime can route requests policy-aware (latency vs cost).
- For latency-critical endpoints (batch=1): optimize host-side executor (C++ path) to reduce kernel enqueue overhead; consider a small local microbatching + immediate flushing heuristic.

Next steps / TODOs:
- [Priya] Add the full raw trace artifacts to the Confluence page and attach Nsight captures (due 2026-03-08).
- [Ethan] Re-run A100 tests with CUDA 12.0 and capture cuBLAS versions to isolate regression (due 2026-03-07).
- [Miguel] Investigate bitsandbytes warnings on H100 builds and confirm quantized correctness (ENG-1255).
- [Sara] Validate Hosted AMI images for L40S with driver 545.x and run smoke tests for p95 stability across regions (due 2026-03-10).

Appendix (quick notes / scratch):
- Command snippet used for throughput runs: 
  docker run --gpus all --ulimit memlock=-1 --shm-size=1g 
  -e CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 
  -v /data/bench:/work/bench redwood/serving-bench:ci-20260302 
  ./bench_runner --model 13b-bf16 --seq 2048 --batch 8 --warmup 3000 --duration 120 

- Profiling tips: use Nsight Systems with --capture-range=process to avoid host noise; for kernel-level use nsight-compute on a single GPU under low contention.
- Trace storage: S3 bucket redwood-bench-results/2026-03-05/ has zip files (links added to Confluence page).

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this doc iterative — more raw numbers to add. Some runs are still queued on p5/g5dn SKUs.
- We may want a short intern project to automate driver/stack sweep across many SKUs (costly but valuable).

End of working doc.
